mistakes.text: By Friday she will finish every exercise on the rings.
mistakes.normalized: by friday she will finish every exercise on the rings
mistakes.feedback_sk: „By Friday“ znamená hotové do piatku, preto Future Perfect: „will have finished“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: „By Friday“ znamená hotové do pátku, proto Future Perfect: „will have finished“.
mistakes.feedback_en: “By Friday” means complete before then, so use the Future Perfect: “will have finished”.

mistakes.text: By Friday she will have finish every exercise on the rings.
mistakes.normalized: by friday she will have finish every exercise on the rings
mistakes.feedback_en: After “will have” use the past participle: “finished”.

mistakes.text: Until Friday she will have finished every exercise on the rings.
mistakes.normalized: until friday she will have finished every exercise on the rings
mistakes.feedback_sk: „Do piatku“ v zmysle „najneskôr“ je „by Friday“, nie „until Friday“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: „Do pátku“ ve smyslu „nejpozději“ je „by Friday“, ne „until Friday“.
mistakes.feedback_en: “Until” means the action continues up to Friday; for a deadline use “by Friday”.

mistakes.text: By Friday she will have finished every exercises on the rings.
mistakes.normalized: by friday she will have finished every exercises on the rings
mistakes.feedback_en: “Every” is followed by a singular noun: “every exercise”.

mistakes.text: By Friday she finishes every exercise on the rings.
mistakes.normalized: by friday she finishes every exercise on the rings
mistakes.feedback_sk: Dej bude hotový do budúceho termínu, preto Future Perfect: „will have finished“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Děj bude hotový do budoucího termínu, proto Future Perfect: „will have finished“.
mistakes.feedback_en: The action will be complete before a future deadline, so use the Future Perfect: “will have finished”.
